title: equimuse_normuon: optimizer state kept in param dtype → bf16/fp16 params stall (no progress)
description:
## What
All schedule-free / Muon state tensors are allocated with `torch.clone(p.detach(), ...)` and `torch.zeros_like(p, ...)`, inheriting the parameter dtype: `z` (:564), `exp_avg_sq` (:611), `momentum_buffer` (:692). For bf16/fp16 params these buffers are bf16/fp16. The fast-sequence update `z.add_(update, alpha=-lr)` (fallback :676, muon :864) then accumulates a small `lr*update` increment into a bf16 tensor; when |z| is moderate relative to lr*update, increments fall below the bf16 ULP and round away → z does not move and the optimizer makes zero progress. The exp_avg_sq EMA (beta2=0.999) and momentum EMA similarly lose their (1-beta) increments.

The sibling/reference optimizers force fp32 precisely to avoid this: optim_sfplus.py:129 `param.detach().float()`; optim_anchormuon.py:103 `dtype=torch.float32`. equimuse_normuon is the outlier.

## Impact
Fully-bf16/fp16 parameter training (e.g. `model.bfloat16()`, not fp32-master+autocast) silently fails to train. Verified empirically: over 300 steps a bf16 fallback param's z moved 0.0 (fp32: 1.21); a bf16 muon matrix's z moved 0.0078 (fp32: 1.88, ~240x worse).

## Fix
Allocate and maintain all optimizer state in float32 regardless of param dtype (`state['z'] = p.detach().float().clone()`, `exp_avg_sq`/`momentum_buffer` as `dtype=torch.float32`); read grad as `.float()`, do all accumulation/Newton-Schulz in fp32, downcast only on the final write-back into the param.

## Location
workers/codex_equimuse_normuon/equimuse_normuon.py:564, 611, 692 (alloc); 676, 864 (consume)
notes: Started fp32 optimizer-state fix in equimuse_normuon while tokenized HPO continues.
close_reason: Moved EquiMuse fast sequence, SODA anchors, fallback moments, and Muon momentum to fp32 state; added bf16 regression test; EquiMuse tests pass.

title: optim_anchormuon: leading-singleton matrix params (e.g. ViT pos_embed [1,T,W]) misrouted to scalar fallback
description:
## What
The spec/root route matrix params on the *effective* shape after dropping singleton dims ([1,tokens,width] is a matrix; [1,1,width] a vector). The worker does NOT squeeze singletons: `_use_muon_for_param` uses `rows = param.shape[0]`, `cols = numel//rows` (:453-460); `_matrix_view` reshapes to `(shape[0], -1)` (:78-82). Any param with a leading singleton gets rows=1 → min(rows,cols)=1 < min_matrix_dim(2) → routed to the scalar RMS/Adam fallback. Forced onto Muon via `use_muon=True`, `_matrix_view` yields a degenerate 1xN matrix and GramNS orthogonalizes a single row (meaningless direction).

Compare root optimizer.py:_matrix_view (:310-319), which correctly builds effective_shape from non-singleton dims.

## Impact
On the docstring's stated ViT workload, a pos_embed [1,196,768] silently receives an Adam-style fallback update instead of the intended Muon orthogonalized update — diverges from the spec and from the root optimizer.

## Fix
Filter singleton dims before computing rows/cols in both `_use_muon_for_param` and `_matrix_view`: `effective = [d for d in param.shape if d > 1]`, require len>=2, rows=effective[0], cols=prod(effective[1:]); reshape to (rows, cols). Make routing and reshape use identical effective-shape logic.

## Location
workers/codex_noradam_confidence/optim_anchormuon.py:78-82, 453-460
close_reason: Mirrored root effective-shape matrix routing in worker AnchorMuon by dropping singleton dimensions before routing/flattening; added [1,T,C] regression; py_compile and worker AnchorMuon tests pass.

title: optimizer.py: dict matrix param-group doesn't propagate fallback_betas/eps to routed fallback params
description:
## What
In `AnchorMuon._prepare_param_groups`, when the user passes param groups as dicts with `use_matrix_update=True` (or the `use_muon` alias), the matrix branch sets only `fallback_mode` and `fallback_weight_decay` (:633-635) — NOT `betas` or `eps`. At step time, any param in that group whose GRADIENT is not matrix-like is routed to `_step_fallback_param` (:803-804), which reads `group.get("betas", (0.9, 0.999))` (:866) and `group.get("eps", 1e-8)` (:867). Because the matrix group has neither key, the fallback update silently uses beta2=0.999 (not the configured fallback_betas, default (0.9,0.95)) and eps=1e-8 (ignoring a user eps). The non-matrix dict branch (:628-632) sets both correctly, so the bug is specific to fallback params living inside a matrix dict group.

## Impact
Medium: only triggers when a user supplies dict param groups with use_matrix_update=True, places non-matrix-grad params there, AND relies on non-default fallback_betas/eps. The from_model/tensor-list/named-tuple paths route fallback params into a separate, correctly-wired group, so common usage is unaffected. Verified numerically: vector trajectory diverges from the correctly-wired path under varying gradients.

## Fix
In the matrix branch (:633-635) also `group.setdefault("betas", fallback_betas)` and `group.setdefault("eps", eps)`, mirroring the non-matrix branch.

## Location
optimizer.py:633-635, 866-867
notes: Started while tokenized FineWeb HPO runs; this root optimizer fix does not touch the active runner.
close_reason: Fixed matrix dict groups to propagate fallback betas/eps and added regression test; tests/test_optimizer.py passes.

title: run_wikitext_llm50m: worker subprocesses don't receive --seed → wrong data seed + concurrent cache-write race
description:
## What
`launch_trials` (:1275-1338) forwards every metric-relevant flag to worker subprocesses EXCEPT `--seed`, so each worker's `parse_args()` falls back to the default `seed=123` (:115). The worker then calls `prepare_text_cache(args)` in `run_trial` (:644). For HF datasets `args.seed` is baked into the cache filename (`...seed{args.seed}`, :311/352) and the streaming shuffle seed (`ds.shuffle(seed=args.seed)`, :322/328/364/370). The worker therefore can't find the parent's `seed{N}` cache and re-streams/re-shuffles with seed 123 — a different train/val partition than requested. Model RNG is unaffected (uses trial.seed), so only the *data* seed is silently wrong.

## Impact
Results recorded under the requested seed were trained/evaluated on seed-123 data; environment.json records the requested seed → silent + unreproducible. Additionally, parallel workers `np.save()` to identical `seed123` paths with no lock (:333-334/375-376) → write/read race that can yield a truncated/corrupted `.npy` read later by TokenStream (:65) as garbage tokens.

## Repro
`--dataset-source hf_text --preset fineweb_long --seed 7`: parent prepares `..._seed7_...`; workers run with seed=123, miss the cache, re-shuffle FineWeb with 123.

## Fix
Add `"--seed", str(args.seed)` to the worker cmd in launch_trials. Have the parent prepare all caches before launch and make workers fail loudly on a missing cache instead of rebuilding. Use temp-file + atomic rename to avoid concurrent-writer corruption.

## Location
run_wikitext_llm50m.py:1275-1338, 644, 311/322/328/352/364/370, 333-334/375-376, 65, 1528/1538
close_reason: Fixed worker seed propagation, worker cache-missing behavior, and atomic cache writes. Workers now receive --seed, require parent-built caches instead of rebuilding, and .npy writes use temp+os.replace. Added tests for atomic save, seed-specific cache requirement, and command seed forwarding; py_compile and tokenized runner tests pass.

title: run_synthetic_llm50m: final_trials_from_hpo KeyError when --max-hpo-trials drops an optimizer family
description:
## What
`hpo_trials()` builds candidates family-ordered (8 adamw/adamatan2, then 4 muon, then 8 anchormuon) and truncates with `trials = trials[:args.max_hpo_trials]`. `final_trials_from_hpo()` then does `row = best[family]` unconditionally for every family in ("anchormuon","adamw","adamatan2","muon"). If truncation removes all trials of a family, `best` (built only from HPO rows that ran) lacks that key → `KeyError` aborts the whole run.

## Impact
`--max-hpo-trials N` (a documented flag, :345, the natural way to do a quick/partial run) crashes the main process AFTER all HPO GPU time is spent. E.g. `--max-hpo-trials 4` keeps only adamw/adamatan2 → `best['anchormuon']` raises KeyError.

## Fix
Guard the loop: `for family in (...): if family not in best: continue`. Or sample `--max-hpo-trials` evenly across families. Or fail early with a clear message if a required family is absent from hpo_rows before launching trials.

## Location
run_synthetic_llm50m.py:604-619, 345
notes: Started after root optimizer fallback fix. Scope: make max-hpo-trials truncation safe in synthetic LLM runner.
close_reason: Guarded final_trials_from_hpo against missing families after max-hpo-trials truncation and added regression test; py_compile and test_synthetic_lm_runner pass.

title: Bug-hunt low-severity findings (16): optimizer/runner/model/test cleanups

title: run_cifar10_ablation: best_by_family selects max-over-seeds (luckiest seed), not per-seed mean
description:
## What
With multi-seed expansion (`expand_trials_by_seeds`, :2385) the family of a config ignores the `_seedN` suffix. In `summarize()`, `by_family` keeps the single row with the max `(best_val_acc, -best_val_loss)` across ALL rows in the family — including every seed (:2244-2249). No mean/std over seeds is computed anywhere. In `--two-stage` that single luckiest (config, seed) is promoted to the finals (:2486-2487).

## Impact
Per-family selection is driven by seed noise rather than mean performance; the per-seed aggregation the runner advertises is never computed → optimistic selection bias.

## Repro
`--preset confidence --seeds 1,2,3 --two-stage`: best_by_family['adamw'] = whichever (config, seed) had the single highest accuracy; that exact config goes to finals.

## Fix
Aggregate per (family, config-without-seed) by mean (report std) of best_val_acc across seeds; select the family winner by mean; carry that config (not a single seed run) into the finals.

title: run_cifar10_ablation: LR schedule silently ignored (and mislabeled) for anchormuon/golden/sfplus trials
description:
## What
The external LR schedule is applied only when `cfg.optimizer in {adamw, root, muown, ema_muon, ema_muown}` or `cfg.external_lr` is True (run_cifar10_ablation.py:1882). For plain `anchormuon` / `golden` / `sfplus` trials (external_lr defaults False), the runner never calls `scheduled_lr`/`apply_scheduled_lrs`. AnchorMuon's internal schedule only does warmup then holds LR constant (optim_anchormuon.py:_group_schedule, ~:412-420) — no cosine/linear/wsd decay. So `cfg.lr_schedule='wsd'|'cosine'` on those trials is a no-op, yet the summary records `lr_schedule=cfg.lr_schedule` (:2015).

## Impact
Ablations compare decayed-LR AdamW baselines against never-decayed AnchorMuon/golden, while the JSON/CSV claim both used wsd/cosine. Comparisons are unfair and mislabeled (affects component_ablation, cifar5_compare, best_cifar10, root_*_ablation, confidence, feedback presets).

## Repro
`--preset component_ablation`: AdamW baselines decay; anchormuon family trials (lr_schedule='wsd') train at constant LR after warmup but are reported as 'wsd'.

## Fix
Set `external_lr=True` for anchormuon/golden/sfplus trials that request a non-constant schedule (so the runner drives LR), or add them to the gate set at :1882, or error/normalize to 'constant' when a non-constant schedule would be silently dropped so recorded schedule matches reality.

## Location
run_cifar10_ablation.py:1882-1892, 1681-1701 (make_optimizer), 1759-1776 (golden), 2015; optim_anchormuon.py:412-420
notes: Started LR schedule correctness fix. Scope: ensure recorded non-constant schedules are applied to AnchorMuon/golden/SFPlus trials or represented truthfully.
close_reason: Made non-constant AnchorMuon/golden/SFPlus schedules trainer-owned, unified the schedule gate, and added regression tests; py_compile and test_cifar_runner_args pass.

title: run_cifar10_ablation: --val-source defaults to 'test' → model selection on official test split (HPO leakage)
description:
## What
`--val-source` defaults to `test` (run_cifar10_ablation.py:143). The help text even notes "Historical runs use CIFAR-10 train=False as validation." In that mode `cifar10_loaders` sets `val_ds = test_full` (:1150), so every val_loss/val_acc — and thus `best_val_acc/best_val_loss`, `best_run.json` (summarize :2192), and `best_by_family.json` (:2244) — is computed on the official CIFAR-10 test split. In `--two-stage`, the configs promoted to the finals are selected on the test set.

Also: with `--val-source=test` the validation subset is `Subset(test_full, range(val_subset))` (:1156) and the final test subset is `Subset(test_full, range(test_subset))` (:1167), so val ⊆ test (default val=test[0:2000] ⊂ test[0:10000]). The "official test evaluated only at the end" metric is then contaminated by data used for selection/HPO.

## Impact
HPO / per-family model selection performed on the official test split = textbook test-set leakage; reported test numbers from default invocations are optimistic/invalid. (The README's 45k/5k/10k flagship protocol corresponds to `--val-source train_split`, so that headline result is likely clean — but the default and "historical"/HPO runs are not.)

## Repro
`python run_cifar10_ablation.py --preset confidence --two-stage` (no `--val-source`). All configs scored on CIFAR-10 test; best_by_family picks winners by test accuracy; finals derived from test-selected configs. Add `--eval-test` and val (test[0:2000]) overlaps the reported test set entirely.

## Fix
Default `--val-source=train_split`, or hard-error when HPO/`--two-stage` selection runs with `val_source=test`. Forbid `--eval-test` together with `--val-source=test`. Reserve `train=False` strictly for a single end-of-run test pass.

## Location
run_cifar10_ablation.py:140-148, 1148-1167, 1939-1941, 2192, 2244-2250, 2471-2486
notes: Started data-leakage fix. Scope: default validation split and guard against HPO/two-stage/test-eval leakage.
close_reason: Changed default val_source to train_split, added supervisor/test-overlap guards, and added regression tests; py_compile and test_cifar_runner_args pass.

title: run_cifar10_ablation: per-seed runs use different train subsets in test mode (confounds seed variance)
description:
## What
In `--val-source=test` mode the training subset is drawn with a generator seeded by the trial/seed value: `subset_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(int(args.seed))` (:1152), and the supervisor passes the per-seed value into `--seed` (:2106). So two seeds of the same config train on DIFFERENT 10k subsets of CIFAR-10 train. In `train_split` mode the subset is drawn from the fixed `split_gen` (split_seed) so all seeds share the same data (:1131-1137).

## Impact
In the default test mode, "seed variance" mixes optimizer-init/dropout RNG variance with train-data-resampling variance, and the two val-sources aren't comparable across seeds — across-seed spread overstates true optimizer variance.

## Fix
Seed the train-subset draw from a fixed data seed (e.g. args.split_seed) in test mode too, independent of the trial seed, so all seeds of a config see the same training data.

## Location
run_cifar10_ablation.py:1151-1154, 1131-1137, 2106
close_reason: Fixed test-validation train subset sampling to use split_seed instead of trial seed and added a regression test showing identical subsets across different trial seeds; py_compile and tests/test_cifar_runner_args.py pass.

title: run_cifar10_normuon_aspect_ablation: GPU launcher round-robin oversubscribes a busy GPU on out-of-order completion
description:
## What
GPU assignment uses `env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str(next_gpu % gpu_count)` with `next_gpu` incremented once per launched trial (:535-536). The scheduler never tracks which physical GPU is free — only a count (`while pending and len(running) < gpu_count`, :491). When trials finish OUT of round-robin order, the freed GPU is not the one the modulo counter selects, so a new trial is pinned to a still-occupied GPU while the actually-free GPU idles. Violates the docstring's "one trial per visible GPU" invariant.

## Impact
With more trials than GPUs and heterogeneous runtimes (e.g. `--preset tune` 13 trials or `--preset peer_final` 8 on 4 GPUs; AdamW ~1.8x faster than soda), two batch-512 ViT trainings can share one GPU while another idles — halved throughput at best; OOM (non-zero exit) → `raise SystemExit` (:548-549) aborts the whole sweep at worst.

## Fix
Track free GPUs explicitly: `free_gpus = list(range(gpu_count))`; pop on launch and store the id in the `running` tuple; return it to the pool when a process finishes. Assign CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES from the popped id, not `next_gpu % gpu_count`.

## Location
workers/codex_soda_pmuoneq_normuon/experiments/run_cifar10_normuon_aspect_ablation.py:489-541
close_reason: Replaced round-robin GPU assignment with an explicit free-GPU pool so out-of-order trial completion reuses the actually freed GPU; py_compile passes.

title: Investigate Muown CIFAR instability and underperformance
description: The 2026-06-01 CIFAR-10 transfer check found Muown underperformed AnchorMuon and EMA-Muown no-weight-decay HPO trials produced NaNs around epoch 3. Follow-up: audit the local CifarMuown implementation against the paper/reference code, add targeted numeric tests for the row-magnitude parameterization, and only then decide whether CIFAR needs more HPO.
